references.text: The context for the prohibition against offering animals with defects, which also applies to animals from foreigners
Parallel regarding defects that disqualify, here concerning priests with physical impairments who cannot present offerings
Reiterates the prohibition against offering animals with defects to the Lord your God
Prohibition against offering animals with defects or anything evil, as this is an abomination to the Lord
The requirement that sacrificial animals must be without defect to be accepted by the Lord
Requirement for a defect-free animal in peace offerings
Malachi rebukes the people for offering blind, lame, and sick animals, which violates the requirement for unblemished sacrifices
Condemnation of one who promises a good animal but offers one with defects
Ezekiel warns against allowing foreigners who are uncircumcised in heart to serve in the sanctuary and profane God's house
